items.headline: AI-driven polymer discovery could replace years of trial and error with closed-loop testing
items.excerpt: Researchers propose a closed-loop polymer-discovery ecosystem that links databases, predictive models, AI agents, simulations and automated labs to compress years of trial-and-error materials work into much faster cycles.

items.headline: AI-informed AdaptiveFlow redefines large-scale cloud computing for drug discovery
items.excerpt: Scientists from St. Jude, the University of Pavia, Dana-Farber and Harvard unveiled AdaptiveFlow, an AI-informed platform that can virtually screen billions of drug-like molecules at roughly 1,000-fold lower computational cost than existing ultra-large screening methods.

items.headline: Hot subdwarfs come into focus as AI scans thousands of stars in Gaia data
items.excerpt: A new project that began this September uses AI to scan thousands of stars in Gaia's catalogue to identify rare hot subdwarf stars, with the effort set to expand sharply once Gaia DR4 is released in December.

items.headline: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
items.excerpt: A live recording from the International Congress of Mathematicians examines what mathematicians value about doing math as AI systems increasingly generate proofs and tackle open problems.

items.headline: In an Age of AI, a Physicist Seeks What Endures
items.excerpt: Yale physicist Sarah Demers, who is drafting an American Physical Society policy statement on AI, weighs the technology's risks against emerging benefits, including an AI system that helps control the Mu2e experiment's search for a rare muon-to-electron transformation.

items.headline: Brain-Computer Interface Aligns Better with Humans via AI
items.excerpt: New research shows that combining human motor learning with AI improves brain-computer interface calibration and performance, offering hope for people who have lost the ability to move or speak.
